sequence_strategy: Rodrigo Castillo asked us for help, so Email 1 replies in his own thread the same business hour. It repeats his request back (three 24/7 Atacama lithium sites, costly and hazardous contracted crews, the Anglo American referral, a Q3 budget conversation), gives one proof point that no other vendor has (SQM's own iodine operation already runs FlytBase with Adentu, S1), asks two questions and offers two Santiago-time slots. Each follow-up targets a different Stage 1 gap and adds one new thing: Email 2 covers Decision Criteria with how the iodine setup handled desert connectivity and IT. Email 3 covers Decision Process with a forwardable five-bullet summary for his safety, IT and finance colleagues, tied to SQM's stated safety commitment. Email 4 closes the loop around Paper Process and offers to hold until before his Q3 budget conversation, so the ask gets smaller as he stays quiet.

tone_adaptation.seniority: He is Head of Operations, so the emails are brief and peer-level and lead with outcomes (crew safety, coverage, cost). They contain no feature lists or specs. Each has one ask, and the call is short (30 minutes) with an open invitation to bring a safety or IT colleague.
tone_adaptation.industry: Mining: the emails talk about crew exposure, around-the-clock coverage of remote sites and desert reliability (heat, dust, connectivity), with acronyms spelled out. The proof is a peer deployment in the same desert and company (S1), and the safety framing uses SQM's own stated commitment to accident-free operations (S18), rather than generic drone benefits.
tone_adaptation.stated_context: Chile: formal 'Dear Mr. Castillo', a diplomatic and unhurried tone, and the trusted introduction (Anglo American) named in the first line. Times are in America/Santiago, and Email 1 offers to continue in Spanish. His Q3 budget conversation is the timeline anchor: Email 3 offers a pilot scope for it, and Email 4 offers to hold until then rather than pushing.

emails.send_when: Within 1 hour of the inbound, Friday 6 November 2026, Santiago business hours, as a reply in his original thread
emails.goal: Confirm we understood his request, establish relevance with SQM's own deployment and book a 30-minute discovery call
emails.subject: Re: Autonomous inspection for our Atacama lithium sites
emails.body:
Dear Mr. Castillo,

Thank you for your note, and for the introduction through Anglo American. You are looking for drone-based inspection across three large lithium sites in the Atacama that run 24/7, so your contracted crews spend less time in hazardous areas and cost less.

The aim would be scheduled, docked drone flights that cover your sites around the clock, with your team reviewing results remotely instead of sending crews out.

You may know that SQM's own digital innovation team already runs this in the Atacama: with Chilean integrator Adentu, docked drones on FlytBase moved iodine inspections from biweekly to twice daily, with mission reliability above 95% in desert conditions.

Two questions so the call is useful to you:
1. Which inspections take the most crew hours today, and how often do they run?
2. Who else will join your Q3 budget conversation, and should Rodrigo Toler's team be part of it?

Would Tuesday 10 November at 10:00 or Wednesday 11 November at 15:00 (Santiago time) work for a 30-minute call? You are welcome to bring a safety or IT colleague.

Con gusto podemos continuar en español.

Kind regards,
Samruddhi Sontakke
Business Development, FlytBase
emails.why_this_email_now: He wrote to us with a clear need, a warm referral and a budget date, so a fast reply that is specific to him is what earns the meeting. The strongest relevance we have is that his own company already runs FlytBase in the same desert (S1), so that is the single proof point. BDR notes: [NEED: confirm deal registration and channel position with Adentu before sending, because Adentu is SQM's incumbent integrator (Stage 5)] [NEED: the case study's iodine yield figure is inconsistent (2% vs 4x), so it is left out] [NEED: direct phone and email in the signature block] [NEED: which business unit 'Northern Operations Division' is (Novandino lithium or iodine); public sources do not name it] [NEED: the Anglo American Quellaveco case (Stage 4, S2) is not in the kept Stage 2 research, so it is not cited in the emails; the BDR can attach it after checking].
emails.why_next: If he does not reply, Email 2 answers the question an operations head asks next (will it work in our conditions?) and moves to Decision Criteria.
emails.success_signal: He accepts a slot or proposes another time, or answers either question (crew hours or frequency, Q3 participants).

emails.goal: Address desert reliability and IT fit and surface his technical decision criteria
emails.subject: Re: Autonomous inspection for our Atacama lithium sites
emails.body:
Dear Mr. Castillo,

One detail on Atacama conditions, since heat, dust and connectivity usually decide whether docked drones work at remote sites. In SQM's iodine operation, Adentu connected the docks over Starlink and sent RGB and thermal imagery straight into SQM's Azure environment for analysis: https://flytbase.com/case-studies/sqm-678-km2-mine-autonomous-inspection-adentu-and-flytbase

What would a platform need to prove at your three sites before you would trust it to replace a crew round? If a call is easier, Thursday 12 November at 11:00 or Friday 13 November at 10:00 Santiago time both work.

Kind regards,
Samruddhi Sontakke
Business Development, FlytBase
emails.why_this_email_now: After the proof point, the natural objection from mining operations is whether it works in their conditions and with their IT. This answers that with SQM's own connectivity and data path (S1) and asks him to name his criteria. That fills the Decision Criteria gap, which is still unknown.
emails.why_next: Email 3 switches angle to the people around him (safety, IT, finance) and to the steps before Q3, giving him something he can forward.
emails.success_signal: He names requirements (connectivity, dock count, BVLOS, integration with site systems) or picks a slot.

Dear Mr. Castillo,

In case it helps with colleagues, here is a summary you can forward:
- Need: inspection at three 24/7 Atacama lithium sites without sending contracted crews into hazardous areas.
- Approach: docked drones flying scheduled missions, reviewed remotely.
- Safety: fewer people in the field, in line with SQM's commitment to accident-free operations.
- IT: SQM's iodine operation already sends drone imagery into Azure.
- Next step: a one-site pilot scoped before your Q3 budget conversation.

Would a short call next week to map the steps to Q3 still be useful, perhaps with your safety or IT colleague?

Kind regards,
Samruddhi Sontakke
Business Development, FlytBase
emails.why_this_email_now: Enterprise mining purchases go through safety, IT, supply chain and finance, and the research shows the Atacama assets now sit under a Codelco-SQM joint venture with its own governance (S12, S13). A forwardable five-bullet summary helps him act as champion internally, and framing safety with SQM's own stated value (S18) gives his colleagues a reason they already accept. The ask is smaller (a yes or no to a short call).
emails.why_next: If he is still quiet, Email 4 stops the active sequence, offers to hold until his Q3 timeline and asks only how procurement would run.
emails.success_signal: He forwards the summary, copies a colleague, describes the steps (pilot, committee, tender) or agrees to a call.

emails.send_when: +13 business days, Wednesday 25 November 2026, 11:00 Santiago time, same thread

Dear Mr. Castillo,

I will close the loop here for now, as the timing may suit you better closer to your Q3 budget conversation. Should I check back a few weeks before then, or is a colleague in supply chain better placed to explain how SQM would buy this, for example through a local integrator such as Adentu or a tender?

emails.why_this_email_now: Three unanswered touches mean the timing is wrong, not that he lacks interest. His stated trigger is the Q3 budget conversation, so offering to hold until then respects it, and the single question surfaces the Paper Process (integrator or tender) and whether he will champion it or hand it on.
emails.why_next: End of the active sequence. With no reply, the lead moves to value nurture every 4-6 weeks (case study, implementation approach, objections, scoped pilot), with one refreshed touch timed before his Q3 budget conversation.
emails.success_signal: He gives a date to check back, names a procurement colleague, or describes the buying route.
